clue.text: Ultimate piece of software used in onscreen search

indicators.note: something used in a structure is set inside it, so one letter goes into the other piece

parts.note: read as two words: ON, plus screen meaning cover (to screen is to shield or cover)

indicators.note: the ultimate piece of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A computer user hunts for something on their monitor with the latest bit of software.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ultimate piece of' takes the E at the end of software; 'used in' puts it inside ON COVER, read from 'on screen', where screen means cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a quick inspection or look round, the kind of cursory examination a search can be.

clue.text: Mass of gravel used to be stored in old dilapidated hut

indicators.note: something stored in a place is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other
a dilapidated building is falling apart, so the letters of hut are rearranged

parts.note: used to be means was

explanation.surface: Someone recalls that a heap of gravel was once kept in a broken-down old shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Outwash is the sand and gravel deposited by meltwater streams flowing out from a glacier.

clue.text: Scoundrel restrained when out of bed.

indicators.note: out of means without here, so the letters of bed are taken away

parts.note: restrained means curbed

explanation.surface: A villain was held in check whenever he got up from his bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cur is a contemptible man, a synonym for a scoundrel, borrowed from the word for a mongrel dog.

clue.text: Tax deliveries by transport

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries, so deliveries suggests overs
a train is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A levy is charged on goods delivered by rail or road.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled, or 'delivered', by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: To tax someone is to strain them, and to overstrain is to tax beyond what is reasonable.

clue.text: Dangerous creature transported by alien vessel

indicators.note: something transported by a carrier is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ET, the film's extra-terrestrial, is crossword shorthand for an alien
a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: A deadly animal is carried about in a spaceship from another world.
explanation.definitionFit: An E-boat was a German fast motor torpedo boat of the Second World War, a type of naval craft.

clue.text: Raise useless young animal

parts.note: bum is slang for worthless or useless, as in a bum deal
a pup is a young dog, seal and so on

explanation.surface: Bringing up a feckless young creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To bump up is an informal phrasal verb meaning to increase or raise a price or figure.

clue.text: Second-hand American edition

explanation.surface: A bookseller offers a pre-owned copy of a book published in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Used goods have had a previous owner, which is exactly what second-hand means.

clue.text: Soft drink served up with food, as expected

parts.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning soft

indicators.note: in a down clue served up means the word is written upwards, so cider runs backwards

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink
table means food provided, as in keeping a good table

explanation.surface: A gentle soft drink is brought out with a meal, just as you would anticipate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' writes CIDER upwards in this down clue, giving REDIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something predictable happens just as one would anticipate, so the phrase can stand in adjectivally.

clue.text: In seaside venue, everyone's more friendly

indicators.note: In here places one piece inside another, the everyone piece going inside the seaside venue

parts.note: a pier is a resort attraction at the seaside
everyone's, as in everyone is, gives all

explanation.surface: Out on the seaside promenade, people are all getting along better.
explanation.definitionFit: Pally is informal for friendly, so its comparative means more friendly or chummier.

clue.text: Go on and on consuming port in superior office

indicators.note: a word consuming another swallows it, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: to prate is to chatter on at length
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A tiresome talker rambles on about a harbour in a senior manager's room.
explanation.definitionFit: A priorate is the position or term of a prior, the head of a religious house, so a senior post.

clue.text: Ordered mature cheese and roll to be cut for supper?

indicators.note: letters ordered are put into a new arrangement, so these words are rearranged
a word to be cut is shortened, losing its final letter here

explanation.surface: A diner asks for aged cheese and a bread roll sliced for the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cut' drops the last L of roll, leaving ROL; 'Ordered' rearranges that with MATURE CHEESE. The question mark admits that supper need not be so grand.
explanation.definitionFit: Supper is an evening meal, and one with starter, main course and dessert is a hearty example.

clue.text: Charge copper with it during lawsuit

indicators.note: during places these letters within the lawsuit word

parts.note: an action is a legal proceeding
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: A police officer with sex appeal is caught up in a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts CU and SA inside ACTION; 'it' as SA (sex appeal) is an old convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusation is a formal claim of wrongdoing, which is what a criminal charge amounts to.

clue.text: Nicer lights flicker for this Advent service

indicators.note: lights that flicker move about unsteadily, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Gentler candlelight flickers at a church service in the run-up to Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flicker' rearranges NICER LIGHTS; the surface fits too, since the service centres on lit candles.
explanation.definitionFit: A Christingle is a children's church service held in Advent or at Christmas, with candles in oranges.

clue.text: Circulating six old pence, current share of profits

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the letters for six and old pence turn back

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
d was the symbol for a penny in pre-decimal British money
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Old coins in circulation make up a present-day slice of the profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circulating' turns VI and D round to give DIV, then I follows. d stood for a penny before British decimal currency in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: Divi is informal British shorthand for a dividend, a payout of a company's earnings to its members.

clue.text: Heard chivalrous pair sleep well!

indicators.note: heard signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: two chivalrous men, a knight and another knight

explanation.surface: Two gallant gentlemen were overheard wishing each other a restful night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heard' tells you to say KNIGHT KNIGHT out loud; the silent K disappears.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the everyday bedtime farewell, a cosy way of wishing someone a good night's rest.

clue.text: Woman's love for Namibians?

parts.note: her is the possessive pronoun for a woman
Eros is the Greek god of love

explanation.surface: A lady's affection for people from south-west Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: the Herero are just one people of Namibia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Herero are a Bantu-speaking people living mainly in Namibia, so they are some of its inhabitants.

clue.text: Purser is reeling in shock

indicators.note: someone reeling staggers about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A ship's officer is staggering from a nasty jolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise is an unexpected event that startles, which is a mild sense of a shock.

clue.text: One flying to Rome, initially following a route taken by Caesar

indicators.note: following places the later words after the earlier ones in the answer

parts.note: via is Latin for road or way, the route a Roman would take
taken as written

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pilot heads for the Italian capital, retracing an old Roman road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' signals that the later pieces come after the earlier ones in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aviator is a pilot, a person who flies aircraft.

clue.text: For a lady, top alternative to taxi rank?

parts.note: a bus is another way to get around instead of a cab
a tier is a row or rank

explanation.surface: Is a bus queue a woman's best substitute for a cab rank?
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like a verb or a superlative but is the garment; 'rank' looks like part of 'taxi rank' but stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A bustier is a close-fitting strapless bodice worn as a woman's upper garment.

clue.text: Sort of clip a canine

definitions.meaning: a strong spring clip for holding papers together
a sturdy breed of dog with a flat face

explanation.definitionFit: A bulldog clip is a strong sprung metal paper clamp, and a bulldog is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Former husband, one given part in show

parts.note: ex means former
I is one in Roman numerals
a bit is a part of something

explanation.surface: A woman's ex-husband is cast in a role in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Former husband' as one idea, but it splits into EX and H.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit something is to show or display it publicly.

clue.text: See cyclists on these about to enter French town

indicators.note: a word told to enter another goes inside it

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Watch the bikers ride past on their way into a town in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourers are touring bicycles built for long rides, so you see riders aboard them.

clue.text: Woman oddly not included among floozies

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are left out, so only the even ones of the word remain

explanation.surface: A lady pointedly kept out of a group of loose women.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of floozies.
explanation.definitionFit: Lois is a woman's name, as with Lois Lane, Superman's companion.

clue.text: Not starting continental deer, say, or veal dish

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: someone from the continent of Africa is African

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken, so its sound counts

parts.note: a doe is a female deer

explanation.surface: A gourmet weighs up an exotic deer against a classic dish of veal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not starting' cuts the A from AFRICAN; 'say' has DOE spoken, spelt DEAU, as at the end of the dish's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fricandeau is a French dish of larded veal, braised or roasted and glazed.

clue.text: Have debts: if creditor's about, crouch in fear

indicators.note: about here means around, so the creditor letters go round the other piece

parts.note: CR is an abbreviation for creditor
to have debts is to owe

explanation.surface: A borrower cringes when the person he owes money to comes round.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to shrink down in fright, which is what crouching in fear describes.

clue.text: Make slow progress in Scottish island

definitions.meaning: to edge along a little at a time
in Scottish place names a small island, from Gaelic innis

explanation.definitionFit: To inch forward is to edge ahead slowly, and in Scotland an inch is a small island.

clue.text: Dispense with sexton's services, perhaps, and head for trouble

definitions.meaning: a sexton digs graves, so you might do the digging yourself instead
to act in a way that brings about your own ruin

explanation.definitionFit: A sexton digs graves, so doing it yourself saves his fee; the idiom means bring about your own downfall.

clue.text: Advantages of publicity?

definitions.meaning: in tennis scoring the point after deuce is called advantage, shortened to ad
advertisements, the notices that promote goods

explanation.definitionFit: In tennis 'ad' is short for advantage, and ads are advertisements, the publicity for products.

clue.text: Travel article by European writer

parts.note: to go is to travel
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A trip piece on the continent is penned by a European author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means beside, so E sits next to THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was the great German poet, novelist and dramatist, author of Faust.

clue.text: Condition favouring individual enlisted by news agency

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of

indicators.note: a recruit enlisted by an organisation joins it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: TASS is the Russian state news agency
I as a single one, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Getting on the staff of a wire service depends on being a supportive single person.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a protasis is the 'if' clause of a conditional sentence, which states the condition.
